Goethe for the summer semester of 1953. The text, in a slightly modified form, was published in the “Deutsche Universitätszeitung”, in its issue published on October 12 of that year. According to Horkheimer, the new university education must realize the validity of the new goals and tasks of its activities - fundamental and determining for the reconstruction of post-war West Germany as a renewed democracy. title: Value orientations of Ukrainian students during their studies in wartime Ціннісні орієнтації українських студентів під час навчання в умовах війни
text_snippet: Value orientations of Ukrainian students during their studies in wartime Ціннісні орієнтації українських студентів під час навчання в умовах війни The article analyzes the value orientations of Ukrainian students during their studies under wartime conditions and identifies the specifics of their transformation depending on the year of study and the level of higher education. The relevance of the study is driven by the fact that contemporary Ukrainian students function amidst prolonged social instability, full-scale war, security risks, psychological challenges, and shifts in the educational environment, all of which directly affect the system of young people's life priorities. The paper examines the primary directions in the study of student value orientations within Ukrainian and foreign scholarship, tracing the dynamics of Ukrainian students' values across various historical periods and periods of social transformation. The methodological framework of the research includes historical, comparative, and generalizing methods, as well as Milton Rokeach’s Value Survey. title: Development of Emotional Intelligence of Students of Higher Education Institutions Розвиток емоційного інтелекту студентів закладів вищої освіти
text_snippet: Development of Emotional Intelligence of Students of Higher Education Institutions Розвиток емоційного інтелекту студентів закладів вищої освіти The article examines the theoretical foundations of research of emotional intelligence and student adaptation. Based on an analysis of scientific literature, the views of scientists on the concept of emotional intelligence are summarized. An empirical study of the levels of students’ emotional intelligence and manifestations of its components was conducted, the peculiarities of the relationship between emotional intelligence and adaptation of students were analyzed. It was found that students have a predominantly average and low level of emotional intelligence and these students also have a normal level of adaptability. It has been established that emotional intelligence, which encompasses components such as emotional awareness, self-control, empathy and self-motivation, plays an important role in ensuring harmonious interaction with the environment, reducing stress levels and successfully adaptation to new conditions of the educational environment. The best-developed component is emotion management, with the lowest scores observed in the areas of interpersonal awareness and emotion recognition. text_snippet: Digital transformation of education: challenges for higher education Цифрова трансформація освіти: виклики вищої школи The article examines the features of the digital transformation of the higher education system of Ukraine in the context of the development of the digital economy and the information society. The main trends in the digitalization of the educational environment are identified, the key challenges that arise in the process of introducing modern information and communication technologies into the activities of higher education institutions are analyzed, and the prospects for the development of a digital university in modern conditions are outlined. As a result of the study, it was found that the digital transformation of education encompasses not only the technical update of the educational process, but also a comprehensive change in approaches to the organization of learning, university management, the professional activities of teachers and interaction between all participants in the educational environment. title: The FAIR principles as the foundation of research infrastructure: a literature review of models for various research fields Принципи FAIR як основа наукової інфраструктури: бібліографічний огляд моделей для різних галузей досліджень
text_snippet: The FAIR principles as the foundation of research infrastructure: a literature review of models for various research fields Принципи FAIR як основа наукової інфраструктури: бібліографічний огляд моделей для різних галузей досліджень This article analyses recent research on the implementation of the FAIR principles, which are becoming a cornerstone of research infrastructure. As a result, it has been established that, in the field of education, there are still no common guidelines for fair management and handling of educational data in accordance with the FAIR principles. At the same time, there are examples of FAIR data models for various fields of research that could serve as a basis for developing such a model for scientific research in the field of education. Therefore, the aim of this article is to analyse existing FAIR data models across various scientific disciplines, compare their approaches, and identify common features and limitations that affect the discoverability, accessibility, interoperability and reusability of data. The article noted the historical nature of the process of separating the interests of the Western individual from the interests and functioning of the state, which had the character of an unnatural alienation of the individual from the existence of the state of Western culture. title: On the Way to Implementing a Personalised Learning Model: The Experience of Karazin University
text_snippet: On the Way to Implementing a Personalised Learning Model: The Experience of Karazin University This article explores the institutional experience of V. N. Karazin Kharkiv National University in developing and implementing a personalised learning (PL) model as part of a broader reimagining of higher education in Ukraine. Situated at the intersection of pedagogical innovation, technological transformation, and socio-political disruption, the study offers a detailed account of how PL can address contemporary educational challenges, particularly in the context of war, digitalisation, and shifting student expectations. The authors provide a comprehensive overview of the university’s strategic and operational initiatives, focusing on the integration of interdisciplinary/interfaculty courses, open educational platforms, hybrid learning models, and flexible individual educational plans. These mechanisms are positioned as practical expressions of a theoretical commitment to learner autonomy, competence development, and lifelong learning. The article highlights the multidimensional nature of personalisation in education, encompassing curriculum design, instructional methodology, student support systems, and institutional culture. title: National and international dimensions of open education policy in higher education
text_snippet: National and international dimensions of open education policy in higher education The article is devoted to the analysis of the essence and main characteristics of open education, its advantages, as well as the role of international and national policy in shaping the development strategy of this direction. The key trends in the integration of open education into the higher education system, improving the quality of educational services and stimulating the innovative development of universities are highlighted. Attention is paid to the international dimension of open education: the activities of UNESCO, the European Union, OECD and other international organizations that define global standards and policies aimed at ensuring equal access to knowledge, creating open educational resources (OER) and supporting distance learning. The features of the implementation of the national open education policy are analyzed using the example of Ukraine, in particular the regulatory framework, digitalization of the educational process, creation of platforms and repositories, as well as participation in international cooperation programs. title: Framework analysis as a tool for identifying social inclusion drivers in higher education (drawn from analytical frameworks designed for UK higher education)
text_snippet: Framework analysis as a tool for identifying social inclusion drivers in higher education (drawn from analytical frameworks designed for UK higher education) The article is dedicated to identification and systematization of factors that shape social inclusion in the field of higher education through the lens of framework analysis. The relevance of research is necessitated by the need to develop and augment social inclusion of Ukrainian society as a means of its social cohesion and resilience during the wartime and in the process of post-war recovery. Universities play a key role in the above process, acting not only as centres for human capital development, but also as platforms for generation of new values and development of inclusive cultures. The goal of the article is to identify the basic elements that act as inclusivity drivers. The goal is achieved by comparison of three analytical frameworks operating and augmenting social inclusion in higher education of Great Britain: University of Hull Inclusive Higher Education Framework, Inclusive Learning and Teaching Framework established by Advance HE, and National Framework for Inclusion generated by General Teaching Council for Scotland. title: Ranking Support for the Strategic Development of Leading Universities: Lessons from the University Revolution in China
text_snippet: Ranking Support for the Strategic Development of Leading Universities: Lessons from the University Revolution in China The article uses the example of China to justify that the use of ranking tools contributes to the effective strategic development of leading universities. Rating diagnostics of the effectiveness of relevant strategic measures makes it possible to identify and demonstrate targeted achievements. To characterize the unprecedentedly rapid and sustainable progress of China's top universities, a comparison is made with the avant-garde higher education of the United States, the world's university leader. The study used data from the objective, specially created in China, Shanghai Ranking for the period of unchanged methodology of its general version (ARWU) during 2004-2025, as well as the sectoral version (GRAS) 2017-2024. Thanks to the ranking assessment, it was found that university development in China occurs simultaneously in qualitative and quantitative dimensions. In terms of the number of universities in ARWU, mainland China (including universities in the special zones of Hong Kong and Macau) will surpass the United States starting in 2022. title: Theodor Adorno. About Technology Аnd Humanism
text_snippet: Theodor Adorno. About Technology Аnd Humanism The article "On Technique and Humanism" (Über Technik und Humanismus) by Theodor Adorno, a German social thinker, university lecturer, and leading representative of the Frankfurt School, was written as an address to his teaching colleagues at Frankfurt University, specifically to instructors of technical disciplines. It was published in the journal Deutsche Universitätszeitung in the issue dated December 7, 1953. In this work, which is one of his first writings on philosophical and educational themes, the Frankfurt philosopher pointed to the critical state of post-war education in the newly established West Germany (FRG). According to Adorno, the educational process was dominated by the value of technical specialties, which fully corresponded to the practical interests of West Germany at the time as it actively rebuilt its industry and economy destroyed during World War II. This shift pushed humanities disciplines in university education into the background. Specifically, it marginalized subjects that can generally be called theoretical, leading to a decoupling of practice from theory—that is, of practical activity from theoretical knowledge. title: Higher Education Institutions in Post-war Reconstruction: Foreign Experience and Opportunities for Ukraine
text_snippet: Higher Education Institutions in Post-war Reconstruction: Foreign Experience and Opportunities for Ukraine Based on a comparative analysis of the priority areas and forms of participation of universities of foreign countries in post-war reconstruction, the dependence of the processes of their institutional restoration on the general context, policy, strategy and key measures implemented by states to rise from the ruins after the war was revealed. A retrospective analysis of the post-war reconstruction of Germany, Finland, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Japan, South Korea, Lebanon, and Iraq was carried out in relation to the reconstruction and modernization of higher education in these countries. It has been found that the success of the reconstruction process depends not only on economic and political, but also on moral factors, which act as either motivators for selfless work to restore the country after the military upheavals, or, conversely, inhibitors of the reconstruction process, causing its inefficiency. title: Digitalisation of the Universal Design for Learning (UDL) model as a means of enhancing inclusivity in higher education
text_snippet: Digitalisation of the Universal Design for Learning (UDL) model as a means of enhancing inclusivity in higher education The need to develop the European Higher Education Area (EHEA) in Ukrainian higher education and create an inclusive learning environment necessitates research into ways of improving technologies and methods for ensuring inclusive and high-quality learning. Contemporary concepts of social development and education for all emphasise the importance of social inclusion for social cohesion and the socio-economic competitiveness of communities and territories, and therefore direct the attention of educators and researchers to the development and use of innovative tools, including digital ones, to increase inclusiveness in education. The article reviews conceptual regulatory and legal acts and international documents that lay the foundation for digitalisation in the field of social inclusion in higher education. Examples of educational infrastructure are given, representing digital learning resources for social inclusion in a multicultural socio-educational environment. title: Max Horkheimer. Concept Of Education
text_snippet: Max Horkheimer. Concept Of Education The work "The Concept of Education" (Begriff der Bildung) by Max Horkheimer, a prominent German social thinker, university lecturer, and the ideological leader of critical theory (the Frankfurt School), is among those philosophical and educational writings in which the philosopher reflects on the social significance of the phenomenon of das Studium. Perceiving the latter as the representation of the ideological essence of German university education, the Frankfurt philosopher outlines his understanding of the meaning of education in general. This text was originally delivered as a rectorial address during the matriculation ceremony for new students at Frankfurt University for the winter semester of the 1952–1953 academic year. The ceremony took place on October 10, 1952, and the text of the speech was subsequently published in the journal Die Neue Zeitung in the issue dated November 22/23, 1952. In his effort to reveal the meaning of university education to the young audience, Horkheimer, as Rector of Frankfurt University, primarily pointed to the historical character of the phenomenon of education, which originates from the cultural sphere of human existence. title: A New Methodology for Evaluating the Effectiveness of Research Activities: the View of Experts in the Field of Social Sciences
text_snippet: A New Methodology for Evaluating the Effectiveness of Research Activities: the View of Experts in the Field of Social Sciences The evaluation of research activities in higher education institutions based on the principles of open science contributes to improving the quality of research, strengthening institutional research capacity, and deepening the integration of Ukraine’s education and research system into the European Research Area and the European Higher Education Area. This article addresses the problem of improving the updated methodology for evaluating the effectiveness of research activities proposed by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine in 2024. The study presents and analyses the results of an expert survey conducted among representatives of the academic community of higher education institutions by the researchers of the Department of University Research Activities of the Institute of Higher Education of the National Academy of Educational Sciences of Ukraine in April–May 2025. title: Integrating emotional literacy into leadership-oriented ESP teaching: a case of psychology students
text_snippet: Integrating emotional literacy into leadership-oriented ESP teaching: a case of psychology students This article aims to justify and implement an interdisciplinary ESP teaching lesson design that develops emotional literacy as a key dimension of leadership competencies in psychology students. It addresses the growing need for integrated emotional and linguistic skills in higher education settings preparing students for emotionally intensive professional roles. The research follows a design-based research (DBR) methodology, allowing for the iterative testing of pedagogical innovations in real-life academic contexts. The focal point is an ESP lesson titled “Feelings and Emotions,” delivered to psychology undergraduates in 2025. The lesson incorporates authentic multimedia, case-based discussions, guided reflection, task-based writing, and interactive role-play activities. Qualitative data drawn from student responses, formative assessments, observation notes, and reflection logs indicate strong emotional engagement, enhanced awareness of emotional vocabulary, and improved interpersonal communication. title: The impact of state ai policies in shaping higher education: the case of Singapore
text_snippet: The impact of state ai policies in shaping higher education: the case of Singapore This article explores the impact of government initiatives in the field of artificial intelligence (AI) on the development of higher education, using Singapore as a case study. In the context of global digital transformation, governments worldwide are actively formulating policies aimed at advancing AI technologies, which directly influence educational systems. Singapore is among the leaders in this field due to its progressive governmental strategies, particularly the National AI Strategy, and various initiatives led by the Ministry of Education, which focus on integrating AI into educational processes. One of the key initiatives is the Smart Nation program, which provides a systematic framework for developing infrastructure to support the implementation of innovative technologies, including AI, across all aspects of citizens’ lives, particularly in education. The study of Singapore’s Smart Nation initiative is particularly relevant, as it represents a crucial component of the country’s digital transformation strategy. title: Social and institutional transformation of a contemporary university: the experience of the University of Genoa
text_snippet: Social and institutional transformation of a contemporary university: the experience of the University of Genoa The article is dedicated to the consideration of the directions of development of a contemporary university based on the experience of Università di Genova (Italy), which presents a rather successful example of the transformation of a European university as a response to existing societal challenges. It is noted that the need for such a transformation is urgent and evident for a university itself, which, having obtained academic, institutional, and financial autonomy, is to prove and demonstrate the importance of the implementation of its functions of providing higher education and conducting academic research, their significance for society as a whole and for the local community in particular. A higher education institution should play a special role in its region, trying to meet the diverse educational and professional needs of students with different employment statuses and different expectations, especially in the context of inclusiveness and active citizenship. title: University as a source of happiness: the impact of learning and interaction on higher education students under martial law
text_snippet: University as a source of happiness: the impact of learning and interaction on higher education students under martial law The article addresses the pressing issue of the impact of learning and the educational environment on the subjective sense of happiness among higher education students, particularly in the context of martial law. It is argued that happiness serves not only as an individual indicator of psychological well-being, but also as a factor of social cohesion and national resilience. Special emphasis is placed on the fact that, despite the difficult circumstances of martial law, engagement in the educational process, participation in learning activities and various events, as well as interaction with peers and the academic community, can become a source of emotional support and internal stability. The theoretical foundation of the study is an interdisciplinary approach to the phenomenon of happiness, integrating perspectives from psychology, pedagogy, and sociology. The article examines the SPIRE model (Spiritual, Physical, Intellectual, Relational, Emotional) proposed by T. Ben-Shahar and interprets it within the context of the educational process. title: Bibliometric Analysis of the Impact of International Research Collaborations: Insights from Social Sciences
text_snippet: Bibliometric Analysis of the Impact of International Research Collaborations: Insights from Social Sciences The paper studies the increasing role of international research collaborations among universities, with a particular focus on the field of social sciences. The study employs bibliometric analysis of literature on international research collaboration in higher education published between 2000 and 2025, identifying the main themes, pathways and contributions of such collaborations on research productivity, quality, visibility, capacity building and other areas, as well as challenges and barriers associated with conducting cross-border research. Through the systematic analysis of 408 peer-reviewed articles sourced from the Scopus database, the study identifies key thematic categories: Research quality, Research Productivity, Policy and Governance, Challenges and Barriers, Higher Citation Scores, Research Visibility, Knowledge Exchange and Innovation, and Research Capacity Building. The analysis shows that international partnerships have global impact and a home country effect, enhance research productivity and improve research quality by integrating diverse expertise, approaches and methodologies. title: Social leadership of the university in implementing social inclusion and community cohesion
text_snippet: Social leadership of the university in implementing social inclusion and community cohesion This article examines the concept of "social leadership" ("educational and social leadership"), its role and significance in the implementation of the "third mission" of universities within the system of ensuring social inclusion and social cohesion. The main directions of social leadership within the territorial location ("on-site") are highlighted. It is substantiated that the social (socio-educational) leadership of the University (HEI) corresponds to the theory of transformational leadership and aims to achieve multimodal goals: moral modelling, vision, charisma, and individualized consideration (Moral Modelling, Visionary, Charisma, and Individualized Consideration). The importance of the socio-humanitarian and educational components for the post-war reconstruction of Ukraine is revealed: "...access to education and learning opportunities are crucial for the recovery of children, families, communities, and post-war development." title: Modern Advertising of Ukrainian Higher Education Institutions: Ethical-Legal and Philosophical-Communicative Aspects
text_snippet: Modern Advertising of Ukrainian Higher Education Institutions: Ethical-Legal and Philosophical-Communicative Aspects The article analyzes current trends in the advertising of Ukrainian higher education institutions (hereinafter HEIs) in the context of the commercialization of education and the digitalization of communication processes. The authors explore the ethical-legal and philosophical-communicative aspects of advertising in HEIs, highlighting the shift from traditional informational messages to branding strategies that incorporate mythologemes and simulacra. These approaches enhance the effectiveness of advertising campaigns but underscore the need for clearly defined regulatory frameworks. The study addresses challenges related to ethical advertising principles, particularly the need to avoid manipulative practices, misinformation, and discriminatory imagery that may distort the social functions of education. Using phenomenological and hermeneutic approaches, case study analysis, and empirical data, the article examines how the advertising of HEIs contributes to shaping their image as intellectual and cultural centers that respond to societal challenges. title: Social Media in Academia: Trends, Preferences, and the Implications for Student Privacy and Customization
text_snippet: Social Media in Academia: Trends, Preferences, and the Implications for Student Privacy and Customization This study investigates the transformative role of social media in higher education, with a focus on trends, student preferences, and the implications for privacy and learning customization. Drawing on a large-scale quantitative survey of 1,820 students aged from 25 countries-including Ukraine, EU states, the US, Africa, and Asia-the research explores how social networks are reshaping both formal and non-formal educational practices. The findings reveal that social media platforms are not only preferred channels for communication and entertainment but are increasingly used for academic purposes such as accessing study materials, participating in group discussions, watching educational videos, and engaging with educational communities. Notably, approximately 30% of respondents use social media for work and studies, indicating a paradigm shift from traditional, teacher-driven content delivery to student-centered, customizable learning experiences. The study reveals the growing importance of non-formal education. title: Coaching Technologies for Unlocking Postgraduate Students’ Inner Potential
text_snippet: Coaching Technologies for Unlocking Postgraduate Students’ Inner Potential This article explores the use of coaching technologies as an effective tool to support postgraduate students in their academic activities amidst modern challenges, particularly in the context of wartime in Ukraine. The study focuses on the difficulties faced by young researchers, including stress, uncertainty about the future, lack of motivation, and underdeveloped organizational skills—factors that hinder scientific productivity and, in some cases, lead to the abandonment of academic careers. Special emphasis is placed on the importance of nurturing talented youth as the intellectual capital essential for Ukraine’s post-war recovery and integration into the global scientific community. Drawing from the author's practical experience, the article presents the application of four coaching methods—the Balance Wheel, Powerful Questions, the Eisenhower Matrix, and Time Blocking—to unlock the internal potential of postgraduate students. The article outlines the specific features of these methods, their implementation stages, and observed outcomes. title: Max Horkheimer. Questions About Higher Education Teaching
text_snippet: Max Horkheimer. Questions About Higher Education Teaching The renowned German social thinker Max Horkheimer delivered his work “Questions Regarding Teaching in Higher Education” as a speech at the German Rectors’ Conference in Kiel on July 31, 1952. Later that year, the text was published in the October issue of Deutsche Universitätszeitung. In this work, Horkheimer continued his philosophical exploration of the phenomenon of university education, building on the conceptual foundation he had earlier outlined through the German philosophical concept of das Studium. At the time serving as rector of Frankfurt University, Horkheimer critically examined the university as a socio-cultural institution of post-war West German society. He argued that the university failed to fully accomplish its fundamental task: educating a new generation of young Germans through the provision of essential knowledge. According to Horkheimer, the educational process was rigidly constrained by enduring traditions rooted in the European Middle Ages. The prevailing dominance of lecturers’ theoretical authority in university lectures hindered meaningful communication between students and their academic mentors. title: Theoretical foundations of innovative development of student entrepreneurship
text_snippet: Theoretical foundations of innovative development of student entrepreneurship The article examines the theoretical foundations of innovative development of student entrepreneurship in the university environment in the context of digitalization and transformation of higher education. It is noted that the formation of entrepreneurial competence of young people is becoming particularly relevant in the context of changes in the labor market and the growth of the role of universities as innovation hubs. The purpose of the study is the theoretical substantiation and systematization of interdisciplinary approaches to the implementation of innovative educational technologies to support students' entrepreneurial initiatives. The key scientific concepts in economics, pedagogy, psychology, philosophy, sociology and management are analyzed, which constitute the methodological basis of the study. Particular attention is paid to such theories as the theory of human capital (Becker), the innovative theory of entrepreneurship (Schumpeter), the concept of open innovation (Chesbrough), constructivism (Piaget), pragmatism (Dewey) and the theory of organizational learning (Senge). title: Personalized Learning in the Context of a Competence-Based Paradigm of Higher Education
text_snippet: Personalized Learning in the Context of a Competence-Based Paradigm of Higher Education One of the challenges facing the Ukrainian education system is organizing a learning framework that takes into account the individual capabilities and needs of each student. This challenge is addressed by the modern model of personalized learning, which creates conditions for developing students' professional interests, allows them to choose an optimal pace, content, and complexity of educational material, and effectively utilizes modern digital technologies to establish an innovative learning environment. The main features of personalized learning include individualization, differentiation, informatization, self-management, alignment with educational standards and students' professional interests, social orientation, flexibility, and formative assessment. The experienced and personal focus of personalized learning aligns with the principles of a competence-based paradigm in higher education. It is argued that combining a personalized learning approach with a competence-based learning model enhances the efficiency of the educational process, and fosters independence, critical thinking, and professional orientation among students. title: Skills Gap & Competitive Development: the problem of competitiveness balance in the “higher education–labor market” ecosystem
text_snippet: Skills Gap & Competitive Development: the problem of competitiveness balance in the “higher education–labor market” ecosystem The article is devoted to the systematic analysis of the skills gap phenomenon and its connection with competitive development on the example of the fields of activity requiring higher education. It is shown that there exists a dichotomy of the skills gap according to the criterion of relative competitiveness of higher education and the labor market: upward gap vs downward gap. Specificity of the skills gap in the case of reproductive functioning and in the case of competitive development or decline, as well as qualitative and quantitative aspects of the skills gap are analyzed. Taking into account the competitiveness of higher education and the labor market, the best world models of effective interaction between universities and employers, the author substantiates a framework model of the level dichotomy of the skills gap according to the criterion of competitiveness in the “higher education – labor market” ecosystem. The natural missionary leadership of true higher education in comparison with the real sector of the economy is argued. The relevant conceptual and terminological apparatus has been supplemented. title: «Zoom Fatigue» in adult education: a pilot study
text_snippet: «Zoom Fatigue» in adult education: a pilot study This paper is devoted to studying the phenomenon of fatigue and exhaustion experienced by learners using Zoom and, more broadly, video-based classes. Its scientific novelty lies in the fact that this phenomenon is examined for the first time in domestic literature. Additionally, the study presents the initial adaptation of the “Zoom Exhaustion and Fatigue Scale” and its application to a Ukrainian sample. The calculated Cronbach’s alpha values for all subscales of the adapted scale meet the requirements of mathematical statistics, confirming its reliability and suitability for further use. Based on a literature review, the main factors contributing to fatigue and exhaustion from video classes are identified as intense eye contact, high cognitive load, constant self-evaluation, and limited physical activity. The results of an empirical study conducted on Ukrainian learners from various groups indicate moderate levels of fatigue across all subscales of the “Video Classes Exhaustion Scale” (overall, visual, social, motivational, emotional). title: Infrastructure as an indicator and subject of assessment in global, industry and specialized ratings
text_snippet: Infrastructure as an indicator and subject of assessment in global, industry and specialized ratings Based on the identification of the importance of the influence of infrastructure on the success of activities and the processes it provides, the article substantiates the feasibility of using it as an indicator for determining innovation potential, as well as a subject of assessment in infrastructure ratings. It is emphasized the need to study these ratings as bases of empirical data representing the importance and role of infrastructure in the innovative development of universities as centers around which innovative ecosystems should be built, which will act as drivers of the development of higher education, modernization of economic sectors, recovery and innovative progress of Ukraine after the end of the war. Global and industry ratings were analyzed, the indicators of which define infrastructure or activities related to its formation and development. The leading infrastructure rankings are characterized, in particular: THE Impact Rankings: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure; Information and communication technologies and University–industry Research&Development collaboration as sub-ratings of WIPO The Global Innovation Index. title: University Technology Transfer in the USA: Organisational Strategies and Functional Practices
text_snippet: University Technology Transfer in the USA: Organisational Strategies and Functional Practices This study explores the organisational design and strategic approaches employed by Technology Transfer Offices in U.S. higher education institutions, focusing on their engagement with industry partners. By analysing data from sources such as the Association of University Technology Managers Licensing Activity Surveys, the research provides a comprehensive overview of how Technology Transfer Offices facilitate the commercialisation of university-based innovations. The study identifies key functional areas within Technology Transfer Offices, including management, licensing, legal, marketing, and administrative support, and evaluates their roles in the technology transfer process. The scientific novelty of this research lies in its detailed examination of the specific strategies used by Technology Transfer Offices to engage industry partners, such as customised licensing agreements, collaborative research ventures, industry-sponsored research programs, and robust networking and outreach activities. title: Theodor Adorno. To the Question: «What is German?» (translation from German, abstract and comments by Vitalii Bryzhnik)
text_snippet: Theodor Adorno. To the Question: «What is German?» (translation from German, abstract and comments by Vitalii Bryzhnik) The outstanding German social thinker Theodor Adorno, a talented university teacher and one of the founders of the critical theory of society (Frankfurt School), wrote his work «On the question: What is German?» as a speech that he read on May 9, 1965. on the German radio (Deutschlandfunk) in the series of radio programs of the same name. In the same year, the text of the speech was published as an article in the August issue of the West German magazine Liberal. title: Ensuring psychological health of the participants in the educational process in the crisis wartime conditions
text_snippet: Ensuring psychological health of the participants in the educational process in the crisis wartime conditions The study raises the issue of ensuring psychological health of participants in the educational process of higher education institutions (HEIs) who carry out educational activities in crisis conditions caused by the military events in Ukraine in 2014 and Russia's full-scale military aggression in 2022. The article examines essential characteristics of the military-political crisis and identifies range of problems that a person faces when making decisions in a crisis situation. Attention is focused on the problem of human resource management during a crisis. Based on the analysis of publications by Ukrainian scholars, the article discusses challenges faced by academic staff and students of Ukrainian universities in the context of war. The higher education institutions that were temporarily displaced from Luhansk and Donetsk regions twice in 2014 and 2022 were analyzed in a particular way as the educational institutions that were affected by negative factors for the longest time and were most affected by the war. title: Students as subjects of the internal system of quality assurance of higher education
text_snippet: Students as subjects of the internal system of quality assurance of higher education On the basis of regulatory documents and the study of the local experience of higher education institutions, we will summarize the main forms of participation of applicants in improving the quality of higher education. A positive influence in the development of the internal system of quality assurance at the level of higher education institutions is the representation of applicants in the register of experts of the National Agency for Quality Assurance of Higher Education. Student self-government actively participates in the formation of the content of education through the discussion of educational programs for the training of specialists, the quality of teaching, the sequence of studying disciplines and the transparency of the assessment of the knowledge of students. Activities of the Student Quality Assurance Agency are summarized. A mandatory component of internal quality assurance of educational programs is the implementation of feedback in the form of studying the opinions of participants in the educational process.
